attempted_claim: Let (M,d) be a complete metric space in which every point is isolated (M discrete, but inf_{x != y} d(x,y) may be 0; not assumed uniformly discrete), and let F(M) be the real Lipschitz-free space over M. Is F(M) 3-Schur, i.e. ca(x_n) <= 3 delta(x_n) for every bounded sequence (x_n) in F(M), where ca(x_n)=inf_n diam{x_k:k>=n} and delta(x_n)=sup_{x* in B_{X*}} ca(x*(x_n))?
decisive_failure: No proof or disproof of the 3-Schur property for complete merely-discrete spaces was obtained; the distortion-growth computation only delimits the published integer-rounding proof and does not constitute an original theorem, counterexample, or classification result.
